question.text: Payment banks licensed by RBI can perform all of the following EXCEPT:

answer.text: Accept savings deposits up to Rs. 2,00,000

explanation.text: The Logic: Payment banks cannot undertake any lending activities. Per the current RBI position (verified 2026-05-15), payment banks can accept savings/current deposits up to Rs. 2,00,000 per customer (raised from the earlier Rs. 1,00,000 limit), issue ATM/debit cards (not credit cards), and provide payment/remittance services. They are designed to promote financial inclusion for low-income households. The Trap: The Rs. 1,00,000 deposit cap is the legacy figure (cited in NISM X-A p.94) and the most common distractor; the current RBI limit is Rs. 2,00,000. The defining feature — no lending — remains unchanged. Cross-Exam Context: NISM X-A (Ch 5) and VII test banking-system structure and payment-bank scope; the current RBI deposit cap should be used over the older workbook figure.
